name: Kang-Petrov Arms KPS-20 Compact 'Housekeeper'
description:
The Kang-Petrov KPS-20 Compact is a pump-action shotgun chambered in 20 gauge with a 14-inch barrel, four-round tubular magazine, and a pistol-grip stock that reduces the weapon's overall length to just over 60 centimeters. The Housekeeper is designed for indoor defense in the tight corridors and small rooms of residential apartments — spaces where a full-size shotgun is unwieldy.

The 20-gauge chambering and shortened barrel produce a wider spread pattern at close range, which compensates for the reduced accuracy inherent in a pistol-grip shotgun. Kang-Petrov specifically designed the Housekeeper for the scenario where a resident rounds a corner in a dark hallway and needs to hit a threat without precise aiming. The wider spread, combined with 20-gauge buckshot's adequate close-range lethality, makes the Housekeeper effective in exactly the scenario it's designed for and questionable in every other situation.

The weapon's compact size allows it to be stored in a closet, under a bed, or in a dedicated wall-mounted quick-access safe — all common storage locations in Mid-tier residential apartments. Kang-Petrov sells the Housekeeper with a wall mount and combination lock, positioning it as a complete home defense system rather than just a firearm.
legality: Legal — standard registration; short-barrel permit may be required
specifications: caliber: 20 gauge effective_range: 15 meters (buckshot) rate_of_fire: Pump-action magazine_capacity: 4+1 rounds weight: 2.4 kg overall_length: 62 cm
tactical_use: A compact shotgun optimized for indoor residential defense. The short barrel and pistol grip enable maneuverability in tight spaces. The 20-gauge buckshot pattern provides a forgiving hit area at room distance. Not effective beyond indoor distances. The pump action provides reliable cycling. Best deployed as a dedicated home-defense weapon stored near the bed or entry point.
cultural_context: The Housekeeper is the Mid-tier answer to the Gray Zone's Homestead-12 — same philosophy of accessible home defense, adapted for smaller living spaces and slightly higher budgets. In Mid residential districts, the wall-mounted Housekeeper safe has become as common as a fire extinguisher, and only slightly more discussed.
story_hooks: A building fire forces residents to evacuate through a stairwell, and one resident brings their Housekeeper. The panic that ensues when they round a corner and meet security coming up is worse than the fire.

Kang-Petrov's quick-access wall safes are found to have a universal override code that was never changed from the factory default. Every Housekeeper in a KP wall safe is accessible to anyone who knows four digits.
physical_description: The KPS-20 is a brutalist slab of matte-black polymer and worn steel, its barrel stubby and menacing under a film of urban grime. The pistol grip is wrapped in cracked rubber, and the tubular magazine shows stress marks from repeated loading; the whole weapon feels purpose-built for desperate, close-quarters work in the dark. Scratches and dents mar its surfaces—evidence of hasty draws from under pillows and quick storage in cramped apartments.
